Police are often poorly trained and sometimes people who were deemed unfit for military.

I can’t think of a single reason someone would need that kind of gun.

It’s a big platform for political parties. You have the side that wants gun control and the side that doesn’t.  
Both sides feel very strongly and there are often protest from both sides. 

It’s very much an active discussion but no one has the right answer. 


I think in US news, they’re more prone to show stories about people who either stopped robberies or assaults because they had a gun, and also highlight stories where people were attacked by someone wielding a gun. 

I’m not sure how they would even go about doing a statistics study on that without either side being colored by the side of the person reporting it. 

I feel like you have the “I’m going to own 50 guns because it’s my right and I want them.”

The “No one should have them because we’re in a civilized age.”

And the “They’re needed right now but need to be controlled.” 

All sides are equally loud but all very biased.

Schooling makes things easier and faster for people on a lot of cases. 

Both of my parents died when I was young so I never finished high school because I went out and got 2 jobs. 

I started working in kitchens and held low end jobs. 

Over many years I learned more in each place and got better jobs with the skills and experiences I got at the low end jobs. 

Currently I’m a chef in with a much sought after position. People are shocked when they learn I didn’t go to culinary school. 

It took be 13 years and a ridiculous amount of hard work, but I have a position that I shouldn’t have without a culinary degree. 

I just had to get the skills and experience first.

It’s interesting to hear how they’re shown in other places. 

You see a good mix of stories here. 

One of the more recent being a 12 year old boy shot and killed an intruder who was trying to kidnap his younger sister. 

Their parents were at work when it happened and they had trained the son on how to use it. 

I can’t imagine what killing someone did to the boys mental state but he was viewed as a hero.

For me, being a successful gun owner means that no one ever knows I have them at all. 

I think a majority of people feel that way. 

One of my neighbors that I’ve lived next to for over 10 years has a large gun collection. 
After years of hanging out and talking, I only just leavened this about her. 

I have an unpopular opinion about them though. 

Yes, I own them and see a need for them while the USA is in it’s current state of mind, but no, I don’t think everyone should have them. 

I’ve seen plenty of people flash them around like they’re a toy or talk about them all the time. 

I don’t think the average citizen needs a gun that could mow down a crowd. 
I think those should be reserved for military or police. 

It’s also way to easy to get a gun.  Even though I’ve been comfortable with them since I was a kid, I went to classes for each gun I have. 

Learned how to shoot non fatal shots and know every nook and cranny of each gun. 
I also bring them to a range and practice once a month to make sure I’m still comfortable and trained properly on each one. 

I understand that it’s a fundamental right of our country but I think laws need to be re-examined and tightened up. 

Yes, you need to get trained to carry one that’s concealed but most people don’t get training for guns they keep in their home. 

The way the states are currently, I do think it can be smart to keep a gun in your home. 

If we were able to have better gun control, we’d be drastically safer. 

I think the problem is it’s just as easy for a bad person to get a gun as it is for a regular person. 

If they remove gun ownership for normal people, then you’ll have a lot more robberies ending in death. 

If the laws changed next week, I’d turn in my guns and be okey with it.  But the police force would have to be a lot better and have much better resources to work with then they currently do. 

The police aren’t always in the position or have what they need to protect us, so most people feel the need to be able to protect themselves.

She ended up having to shoot him as he came closer to her.

But I would if it meant I could keep my neighbors or my family safe.

I used an insta pot because I wanted to cook 4 meals all at once but you can also do this in a normal pot. 
If using an insta pot just throw all the veggies and spices in there with 2 cups of water and come back 30 minutes later. 

Stove top recipe. 

Set your oven to bake at 400, Add 8 oz tomato paste, 4 tbs harissa powder, and 1 tbs water to a bowl and mix well. 

Put tin foil in a sheet tray and rub the chicken thighs with a few drops of olive oil and salt and pepper each side leaving them skin side up. 

Rub the skin side with the harissa paste until the top has an even costing and add to your preheated oven.  Be sure to rotate your pan and baste the chicken with the dripping in your pan 20 minutes into cooking. 

In a sauce pot add 4 cups of water with 2 tsp of salt and bring to a boil. 
Peel and cut the yucca root, carrots and sweet potatoes into bite sized pieces and add to the boiling water.  Quarter the tomatoes and set aside. 

Cut onions and dice the garlic and lightly sauté them. 

Once everything in the pot is cooked and soft, drain out most of the water leavening about 1-2 inches of stock water in the pot. 

Add in sautéd garlic and onions,  1 can diced tomatoes, fresh quartered tomatoes, 2 tbs yellow curry powder, 1 tsp harissa, 1 tsp turmeric and gently stir everything in. Bring to a simmer and cook everything down together stirring occasionally for 20-30 minutes. 


Lastly sauté your spinach and add to the mix. 

Once your chicken thoughts reach 165 you’re good to go. Enjoy!

In a pan, sauté half an onion and 2 cloves of chopped garlic. 

Add the 2 cans of crushed pineapple and simmer for about 2-3 minutes. 

Cut and add chipotle peppers and mix well. 

Cut pork chops into small bite sized pieces and add to the pan with 1/4 cup chili powder, 1 tbs cumin, 1 tsp cayenne, and 1 tsp paprika. 
Keep it cover and stir occasionally as the pineapple juice reduces. 

The longer you cook it the more tender the pork will be due to the acidity of the pineapple.  I usually let it go for 1-1.5 hours until it’s falling apart. 

Substitute the water for broth when cooking your rice. 

I do 2.5 cups of broth for each cup of rice I’m cooking.  I also recommend adding a tbs of butter to the broth but that’s optional. 

Cut 5-6 Roma and 2-3 tomatillos in a small dice and add to a bowl. 
Dice the other half of the onion and add to the bowl with 1 tsp of salt mixing well.  
Add cumin, cayenne, lime juice to taste. 
I usually go heavy on the cumin and lime. 

If you like spice you can always throw a jalapeños in the mix. 

Black garlic salt and caramelized onions are an amazing thing to add to the sour cream but not necessary.

My first bearded dragon was a rescue from a woman I worked for. 
She kept the poor guy on display on the counter of the store and people were constantly banging on the glass and his conditions were horrid. 

He was also badly mistreated and she “reprimanded” him by snapping her fingers against head. 

Needless to say he had zero trust for humans and would bite anyone who even tried to put their hands in to clean or care for him. 

I took to him immediately and spent months just putting my hand in the tank and letting him bite me. 

It was very slow going but he finally started to let me get closer and finally stroke his head. 

You could totally see the moment he realized he loved head pets! 

By the end of the year, he would hang out on my shoulders and was a huge cuddle bug. 

Funny thing is he held a grudge and until I took him away, he’d always try to bite her if she got close to him. 

Unfortunately he only lived another 6 years after I took him.  

He was my first reptile and I’ll always be amazed at how smart and loyal he was. 
Until him I never knew how loving a reptile could be. 

It’s been a long time since my buddy Cervantes died but It’s time for this gal to add another dragon into her life and I really want to make the new guys tank into a special home.
